title: Why getters and controlled methods are preferred over public fields
answer: Public fields allow callers to read and mutate representation directly, making validation and future refactoring difficult. Getters expose information without granting arbitrary write access, while domain methods or carefully designed setters can validate changes and preserve invariants. AeroTopo's `SurveyProject` uses private fields, read-only getters, and named state-changing methods such as `transition`, `imported`, and `quality` instead of generic public setters, which makes allowed mutations explicit.
